# Fintech App Analytics

Four analyses of a crypto-finance app: how new users get through the identity check, how people use the app, which crypto-backed loans get liquidated, and where its card users are.

**Data:** synthetic, generated by [make_data.py](make_data.py). Only the bitcoin prices are real, from [../bitcoin_forecast](../bitcoin_forecast).

| Notebook | Question | Main findings |
|---|---|---|
| [onboarding_funnel.ipynb](onboarding_funnel.ipynb) | Where do new users drop out of the identity check, and who gets rejected? | 4 in 10 sign-ups never finish. 20% of web users stop at the selfie, against about 12% on phones. In Latin America most rejections are blurry document photos. |
| [product_metrics.ipynb](product_metrics.ipynb) | How many people use the app, do they come back, and which products earn money? | About a third of the month's users show up on a typical day. Referred users stay longer (69% active after 3 months, against 55%). Almost all fees come from the exchange. Newly listed meme coins brought a short burst of trading. |
| [card_users.ipynb](card_users.ipynb) | Where are the card users, do their cards get used, and how concentrated is the money? | Poland orders 39% of the cards. Only about 40% of delivered cards get activated in Latin America, against 61% in the EU, and payments there are declined twice as often. The top 1% of card users hold about half the deposits. |
| [crypto_loans.ipynb](crypto_loans.ipynb) | Which crypto-backed loans get liquidated, and when? | Only loans opened at 70% loan-to-value were liquidated (37% of them), in bursts on the days bitcoin fell. |

## Data files

- `users.csv`: 12,000 sign-ups with country, channel, device, and identity check results
- `transactions.csv.gz`: about 390,000 transactions by product (pandas reads the compressed file directly)
- `loans.csv`: 508 bitcoin-backed loans
- `cards.csv` and `card_payments.csv.gz`: about 7,000 payment cards and their payments, generated by [make_cards.py](make_cards.py)

## Tools

Python, pandas, NumPy, matplotlib
